rationale: The candidate is a complete, well-executed HRV grading package and I found no actionable defects. (1) Base question fidelity: every consequential methodology claim in the public question is verified against the installed neurokit2 0.2.13 source — ecg_peaks defaults method="neurokit", correct_artifacts=False (ecg_peaks.py:9); Welch PSD with Hann window, average="mean", scaling="density", detrend=False (signal_psd.py:291-301); max-normalization power /= np.max(power) (signal_psd.py:219-220); default band edges 0.0033/0.04/0.15/0.4/0.5, normalize=True default and interpolation_rate=100 (hrv_frequency.py:17-28). Input claims (header ECG,PPG,RSP, 100 Hz, 30,000 rows) match the recorded input observation (sha256 6a33ff8a..., 1,784,368 bytes) and outcome.json. Undefined-index semantics (HRV_ULF, SDANN2/SDNNI2/SDANN5/SDNNI5 empty) match the reference structural profiles. The only wording nit is the index attribution 'Henrich triangle index' for HRV_HTI, which is a common literature phrasing for the RR triangular index, does not define any quantity differently, and no check depends on the attribution. (2) Source coverage: the materialization ledger accounts for all 7 literal call sites; the four scientific endpoints (hrv_time 25 cols, hrv_freq 10, hrv_nonlinear 60, hrv_indices 95 — the column union) are all retained, peaks deliberately not supplied as an input, data.head presentation-only. (3) Grader: reads reference dynamically (no hardcoded answers, shapes or column lists); exact per-file column-set match by case-sensitive name; empty-field positions matched exactly; tolerance |s-r| ≤ 1e-9 + 1e-9·|r| with a defensible precision basis (byte-identical replay across reference, oracle, independent solution and two repeatability replays; full-precision serialization round trips verified — controller probes p10-p12 plus recorded author diagnostics in catalog operations 0042/0043: round-trip pass, zeros/perturb/rename fail, 1e-13 pass / 1e-3 fail); cross-file identity check ties hrv_indices to the submission's own domain files; no fallback path search (misplaced outputs/ control fails). (4) Controls: 21/21 executed with expected outcomes — reference, recomputed and independently authored alternative all pass byte-identically; empty, misplaced and each per-file omission fail; 12 probes with 9 meaningful wrong solutions (0.5 ms value shift, unnormalized PSD, 3-15% method-settings changes, coherent spectrum reshaping, symbolic swap, cross-file inconsistency, 4096x single-band scaling, NaN token, dropped column) all fail exactly the targeted checks without crashes or malformed-file reliance, and 3 valid alternatives (quoting, 17-digit scientific/fixed precision with column reversal, 25%-of-bound perturbation) all pass. (5) Isolation: oracle isolation run reports 'isolated'; the environment distribution review plus the hash-matched source-literal scan over hrv_time.py / hrv_nonlinear.py / test_pyplot produced zero magnitude findings against the final CSV cells, and no installed distribution bundles the dataset or any HRV answer table. Residual limitations are disclosed and do not constitute defects: cross-stack tolerance portability was not tested (only the pinned stack is installable offline), so the tolerance effectively mandates full-precision serialization, which the addendum's round-trip requirement already states; EOF byte-set beyond a single LF is untested but unambiguous in the public wording. The grader does not read BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR, which is acceptable because it has no input-dependent acceptance branch — every acceptance relation is determined by the reference tables, and the controller verifies input hashes before and after grading.

The only solver input is the raw 30,000-row ECG/PPG/RSP recording; the R-peak intermediate and all four answer tables are withheld. The grader embeds no answers, column lists, hashes or shapes (reference read dynamically from --reference-dir). Installed environments contain only implementation code: the source-literal discovery scan found zero magnitude matches against all final CSV cells, corroborated by the distribution-level inventory and the setup worker's targeted grep (no bundled dataset or HRV result table anywhere in site-packages). The hint scan is a discovery aid rather than an exhaustive semantic audit, but it is consistent with the structural fact that the answers are computed functions of a non-trivial pipeline on the single yielded input, and all HRV-computing modules are mandatory code that the source itself imports; no uninspected candidate could plausibly hold a precomputed HRV table.

source_coverage.rationale: All four scientific endpoints in the source narrative and preparation inventory are retained as graded outputs: hrv_time.csv (call-57-11), hrv_freq.csv (call-66-11, normalize=True which is also the 0.2.13 default), hrv_nonlinear.csv (call-73-16) and hrv_indices.csv (call-84-14), each a distinct interpreted result cell. The source_operations ledger accounts for every literal call site: nk.data (supplied input, byte-identical staging with sha256 verification), data.head (presentation only, no scientific quantity), nk.ecg_peaks (support — deliberately not supplied to the solver so it performs R-peak detection itself, preserving the original science and the sole determinant of the beat population) and the four hrv calls (results; hrv_indices kept as a result rather than redundant because it is a distinct exported, interpreted cell). Exclusions are scientifically grounded: figures rendered by show=True are plot-only (the underlying indices are all exported), peaks/info are intermediates not requested as outputs. No endpoint was recovered after setup needing fresh review, and no eligible branch was dropped or weakened. The offline data-path adaptation (nk.data('/inputs/https/...')) is route-only, documented in trial/source.diff, with two byte-identical replays; the source reads the same staged bytes that are supplied to the solver. Public descriptions of the four files match the hash-verified reference profiles (25/10/60/95 columns, empty fields only at the 5 undefined indices).
